# @ratmath/linalg

> Exact rational linear algebra with fast float previews that sharpen to exact answers. Part of the RatMath Shelf; numbers come from @ratmath/core (peer dependency). ESM, `import * as linalg from "@ratmath/linalg"`.

Generated 2026-11-26 from @ratmath/linalg 0.1.0 at commit 695e162. Paths are relative to the package root (also inside node_modules/@ratmath/linalg/); line links point at that commit. Types: index.d.ts.

## Docs

- [Full docs as one Markdown file](https://ratmath.com/linalg/llms-full.txt): every page below, with its runnable example
- [PDF](https://ratmath.com/linalg/linalg.pdf)
- [Introduction](https://ratmath.com/linalg/index.html): A JavaScript linear algebra library for exact rational arithmetic.
- [Reference](https://ratmath.com/linalg/reference.html): Entries can be numbers, bigints, strings such as "3/4", "1.25" or "0.#3" (Core's literal grammar), or Core Rationals.
- [Exact workbench](https://ratmath.com/linalg/workbench.html): A scratchpad for the library.
- [Fast, then exact](https://ratmath.com/linalg/fast-exact.html): Every operation returns a Refinement.
- [Elimination and solving](https://ratmath.com/linalg/elimination.html): A system of linear equations is a matrix of coefficients.
- [The four subspaces](https://ratmath.com/linalg/subspaces.html): An m×n matrix A sends vectors with n entries to vectors with m entries.
- [Determinants](https://ratmath.com/linalg/determinants.html): The determinant of a square matrix is the signed volume scale of the map it describes.
- [Inverses and fast exact solving](https://ratmath.com/linalg/inverses.html): Row reduce the augmented matrix [A | I].
- [Eigenvalues and eigenvectors](https://ratmath.com/linalg/eigen.html): λ is an eigenvalue of A when A − λI is singular, that is, when λ is a root of the characteristic polynomial det(λI − A).
- [Jordan and canonical forms](https://ratmath.com/linalg/jordan.html): Two matrices are similar (B = P⁻¹AP) when they describe the same map in different coordinates.
- [Orthogonality and least squares](https://ratmath.com/linalg/orthogonality.html): Gram–Schmidt makes a set of vectors perpendicular by subtracting from each its projections onto the earlier ones: q = a − Σ (a·qₖ)/(qₖ·qₖ) qₖ.
- [Factorizations and powers](https://ratmath.com/linalg/factorizations.html): Elimination below the pivots, with each multiplier saved where it cleared an entry, writes PA = LU: L lower triangular with 1s on the diagonal, U the echelon form, P the row swaps.
- [Integer matrices](https://ratmath.com/linalg/integer.html): Over the integers you may only divide when the result stays an integer, so the allowed row operations are swaps, adding integer multiples, and multiplying by ±1.
- [The matrix exponential](https://ratmath.com/linalg/exponential.html): exp(A) = I + A + A²/2! + A³/3! + … solves the linear differential equation x′ = Ax: x(t) = exp(tA)·x(0).
- [Matrix functions](https://ratmath.com/linalg/matrix-functions.html): A function with a power series can be applied to a square matrix by putting the matrix into the series.
- [Nonlinear solving](https://ratmath.com/linalg/nonlinear.html): Nonlinear solvers keep returning to linear algebra.
- [Iterative and eigenvalue methods](https://ratmath.com/linalg/iterative.html): The rest of this library returns exact answers and avoids the classical numerical methods on purpose.
- [Other number systems](https://ratmath.com/linalg/fields.html): Elimination only needs to add, subtract, multiply, divide and tell whether a number is zero.

## Example

PRINT is the docs box's print helper; use console.log elsewhere.

```js
import { det, solve, eigenvalues, teach } from "@ratmath/linalg";
const job = solve([[2, 1, 1], [1, 3, 2], [1, 0, 0]], [4, 5, 6]);
PRINT("float preview:", job.quick.value.x);
PRINT("exact:", job.exact().x.toStrings());
PRINT("det:", det([["1/2", "1/3"], ["1/4", "1/5"]]).exact());
PRINT("golden ratio:", eigenvalues([[1, 1], [1, 0]]).exact().real[1].value.toString(30));
teach.solveSystem([[2, 1], [1, 3]], [1, 2]).steps.map((s) => s.title)
```
